correctness.rationale: Every zero must have exactly one zero neighbor and one 3 neighbor on a 2-regular cycle, giving disjoint 00 blocks with positive runs flanked by 3. Each run contributes integer excess >=0; a zero run of excess 0 is just 3, while excess 2 is exactly 33, 313 or 3113. A total excess of 0 or 2 determines all optimal cyclic words by length congruence. With no zeros, the 2/3 vertices dominate the entire cycle, yielding weight at least \(n+\lceil n/3\rceil\); the remaining orders 4 and 5 are counted directly. Rotational periods and orbit cases follow from the unique defect. Direct exhaustive label enumeration (orders 3–9) and an independent 16-state min-weight cyclic transfer count (orders 3–120) both match. Neither finite computation nor external literature alone is treated as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The multiplicity and classification of all minimum defensive labelings is a natural complete optimization invariant, rather than an arbitrary subcase. A structural zero-pair lemma and sharp excess-defect classification yield one dihedral orbit for every cycle length at least six, as opposed to two or three exceptional small-order orbits. The new exact all-orders sequence and rational series distinguish optimization rigidity and degeneracy beyond the prior-known minimum scalar. No claim of a general arbitrary-graph theorem or computational complexity breakthrough is made.
